hints.body: Replace “only if” and “if” by implication arrows. For “if and only if”, split the statement into its two directions.

hints.title: Try an allowed horizontal line
hints.body: The question places no nonzero restriction on the gradient. Investigate a horizontal line against the strictly increasing exponential graph. Choose its height relative to the exponential at x=0.
hints.recap: Simple allowed parameter choices can test a universal assertion.
hints.pitfall: Check the number and sign of the intersections instead of relying on a rough sketch.

solution:
Statement I claims that a negative solution forces c>1. Take m=0 and c=12. Then 2x=12 has the negative solution x=−1, but c>1 is false. So I is false.

Statement II claims that c>1 guarantees two distinct solutions. Take m=0, c=2. Then 2x=2 has exactly one real solution, x=1, since the exponential is strictly increasing. So II is false.

For statement III it suffices to refute one direction. Take m=0, c=1. Although c≤1, the only solution is x=0, so there are not two distinct positive solutions. Therefore III is false as well. Answer A: none.
knowledgePattern: Refute conditional claims about exponential and straight-line intersections
